# Data

Discuss what parts of the data sets you will work with.

# Question your team will address

Compare the forescast accuracy of ARIMA models in yearly and monthly data (i.e. is the accuracy of monthly or yearly data better?)
1)Test stationarity of the data, if not, use differencing to get it into stationary data, then confirm
2)Fit an ARIMA model to the monthly data 
2) use Autoarima and run diagnositcs on training data (accuracy data)
3) Fit an ARIMA model to the yearly data
4) use Autoarima and run diagnositcs (80%)
5) use accuracy function and compare the accuracy 


What will your team do with the data? You can do many things with the data. The only constraints are that you

* fit ARIMA and ETS models. You can fit other models in addition to these if you want (lm, glm, gam, etc)
* do diagnostics for ARIMA and ETS models
* make forecasts
* test how good your forecasts or compare forecasts (many options here)

Example, "Our team decided to compare the accuracy of forecasts using best fit ARIMA models for WA, OR and CA commercial yearly landings. Our question is whether forecast accuracy is different for simple (1st order) versus 2nd to 4th order ARIMA models."

#Monthly Data organization first
# Create a date column (first of each month)
chinook.month <- chinook.month %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(paste(Year, Month, "01", sep = "-"), format = "%Y-%b-%d"))

# Plot with facets by State
ggplot(chinook.month, aes(x = Date, y = log.metric.tons)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ State, ncol = 1) +  # 3 panels vertically
  labs(title = "Monthly Chinook Salmon Landings",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Log(Metric Tons)") +
  theme_minimal()


chinook.year <- chinook.year %>%
  filter(!State %in% c("Michigan", "Pennsylvania", "Alaska"))

ggplot(chinook.year, aes(x = Year, y = log.metric.tons)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ State, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Chinook Landings by State",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Log(Metric Tons)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



# Filter for Washington state
wa_data <- chinook.month %>%
  filter(State == "WA") %>%
  arrange(Year, match(Month, month.abb)) %>%
  mutate(
    lnreturns = log.metric.tons,
    year = Year,
    month = match(Month, month.abb)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(year, month, lnreturns)

# Calculate split index

split_index <- floor(0.8 * n)

# Create training and test sets
train_wa <- wa_data[1:split_index, ]
test_wa <- wa_data[(split_index + 1):n, ]

#Using Autoarima to fit the model
#WA
library(forecast)

# Convert training data to time series object
train_ts_wa <- ts(train_wa$lnreturns, start = c(train_wa$year[1], train_wa$month[1]), frequency = 12)

train_wa_clean <- train_wa %>%
  filter(!is.na(lnreturns) & is.finite(lnreturns))

train_ts_wa <- ts(train_wa_clean$lnreturns, 
                  start = c(train_wa_clean$year[1], train_wa_clean$month[1]), 
                  frequency = 12)

# Fit ARIMA model
fit_wa <- auto.arima(train_ts_wa)

# Forecast for the length of test set
h_wa <- nrow(test_wa)
forecast_wa <- forecast(fit_wa, h = h_wa)

# Convert test set to time series to match for accuracy
test_ts_wa <- ts(test_wa$lnreturns, start = c(test_wa$year[1], test_wa$month[1]), frequency = 12)

# Check accuracy
accuracy(forecast_wa, test_ts_wa)
# Plot forecast
plot(forecast_wa, main = "Forecast for WA Chinook Salmon Landings", xlab = "Time", ylab = "Log(Metric Tons)")
lines(test_ts_wa, col = "red", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Forecast", "Actual"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1, lwd = 2)

#Now for the yearly returns
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Find the most recent year in the data
most_recent_year <- max(chinook.year$Year)

# Define the cutoff year for the test set (last 10 years)
cutoff_year <- most_recent_year - 10

# Create training data (all years before the last 10 years)
train_or <- chinook.year %>%
  filter(State == "Oregon" & Year <= cutoff_year) %>%
  filter(!is.na(log.metric.tons) & is.finite(log.metric.tons))

# Create test data (last 5 years)
test_or <- chinook.year %>%
  filter(State == "Oregon" & Year > cutoff_year) %>%
  filter(!is.na(log.metric.tons) & is.finite(log.metric.tons))

# Convert to time series for yearly data (frequency = 1 for yearly data)
train_ts_or <- ts(train_or$log.metric.tons, 
                  start = c(min(train_or$Year)), 
                  frequency = 1)

# Fit ARIMA model
fit_or <- auto.arima(train_ts_or)

# Forecast for the length of the test set (5 years)
h_or <- nrow(test_or)
forecast_or <- forecast(fit_or, h = h_or)

# Convert the test data to time series (aligned with forecast period)
test_ts_or <- ts(test_or$log.metric.tons, 
                 start = c(min(test_or$Year)), 
                 frequency = 1)

# Check accuracy
accuracy(forecast_or, test_ts_or)

# Plot the forecast
plot(forecast_or, main = "Forecast for OR Chinook Salmon Landings", xlab = "Year", ylab = "Log(Metric Tons)")
lines(test_ts_or, col = "red", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Forecast", "Actual"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1, lwd = 2)


#CA
# Function to split data and apply ARIMA for California (CA)
forecast_arima_ca <- function(chinook_data) {
  # Find the most recent year in the data
  most_recent_year <- max(chinook_data$Year)
  
  # Define the cutoff year for the test set (last 10 years)
  cutoff_year <- most_recent_year - 10
  
  # Create training data (all years before the last 10 years)
  train_ca <- chinook_data %>%
    filter(State == "California" & Year <= cutoff_year) %>%
    filter(!is.na(log.metric.tons) & is.finite(log.metric.tons))
  
  # Create test data (last 10 years)
  test_ca <- chinook_data %>%
    filter(State == "California" & Year > cutoff_year) %>%
    filter(!is.na(log.metric.tons) & is.finite(log.metric.tons))
  
  # Convert to time series for yearly data (frequency = 1 for yearly data)
  train_ts_ca <- ts(train_ca$log.metric.tons, 
                    start = c(min(train_ca$Year)), 
                    frequency = 1)
  
  # Fit ARIMA model
  fit_ca <- auto.arima(train_ts_ca)
  
  # Forecast for the length of the test set
  h_ca <- nrow(test_ca)
  forecast_ca <- forecast(fit_ca, h = h_ca)
  
  # Convert the test data to time series (aligned with forecast period)
  test_ts_ca <- ts(test_ca$log.metric.tons, 
                   start = c(min(test_ca$Year)), 
                   frequency = 1)
  
  # Check accuracy
  accuracy(forecast_ca, test_ts_ca)
  
  # Plot the forecast
  plot(forecast_ca, main = "Forecast for CA Chinook Salmon Landings", xlab = "Year", ylab = "Log(Metric Tons)")
  lines(test_ts_ca, col = "red", lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", legend = c("Forecast", "Actual"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1, lwd = 2)
}

# Apply the function to California data
forecast_arima_ca(chinook.year)
